facts.text: Waterford village is the oldest incorporated village in the U.S., incorporated in 1794 before the town was formed.
The town sits at the confluence of the Hudson and Mohawk Rivers, where the Erie Canal’s easternmost locks, the Waterford Flight, connect to the Hudson.
During the industrial revolution, Waterford became a manufacturing hub thanks to its location at the confluence of the Hudson, Mohawk, Champlain, and Erie Canals and three railroad lines.
The Eddy family shaped Waterford’s industrial past; Isaac Newton Eddy founded Franklin Ink Works in 1831, and his son George Washington Eddy built the Hudson and Mohawk Foundry.
Waterford hosts annual Canal Fest and Tugboat Roundup celebrations that honor its canal heritage.
The Northside Historic District and Peebles Island are listed on the National Register of Historic Places, preserving the town’s 19th‑century industrial architecture.
